title: 8-round AES-256 impossible-differential key recovery, improved Phan construction

display.name: Impossible differential, Phan line, low data

target.description: 8 rounds of standard AES-256 with initial AddRoundKey and final MixColumns omitted. The source reports complete master-key recovery, using impossible-differential subkey elimination followed by key-schedule completion or trial encryption.

setting.key_relation: One fixed unknown AES master key; no related-key oracle.
setting.key_population: general secret key; no weak-key restriction reported
setting.plaintext_model: chosen-plaintext structures with a varying inverse-shifted column and fixed other bytes; compatible pairs are selected after encryption
assumptions: Uses the four-round impossible differential of Proposition 1 with input/output extension and early rejection of wrong key guesses.

Reuses three column choices. After filtering, about 2^149 candidate 192-bit subkey guesses are completed with 64 remaining bits, at about 2^213 trial encryptions. The final published time is dominated by 2^229.7 memory accesses.

Section 2's textual AES-256 key-schedule description includes a rotation in the i=4 mod 8 branch; the canonical AES specification has an unrotated SubWord there. This source description discrepancy remains flagged for full-version checking; no alternative cipher is silently substituted.

time.note: Source final 2^229.7 MA (192+37.7). At intermediate D=2^90.7 it separately gives 4·2^128·2^57.7·2^32·2=2^220.7 MA for Steps 3–4; wrong-guess survival 2^-43 leaves 2^149 candidates, with 2^64 completion each costing about 2^213 trial encryptions. Three column-pair repetitions reduce final D to 2^89.1 without multiplying the reported total time. These are stages of one endpoint, not coordinate-wise minima from different attacks.

data.note: Final source-reported chosen-plaintext budget for this instance and endpoint; distinct from intermediate pre-optimization counts.

memory.note: Dominated by storing the 2^96-pair table, as stated on p.290.

preprocessing.note: Section 4.2 explicitly reuses the 2^96-pair table while k5,Col(2,3) is fixed; generating all such tables costs about 2^64·2^96 encryptions of two columns for two rounds. Appendix A additionally constructs and sorts the 2^42-pair elimination table. Neither count is silently changed into full AES encryptions or a complete combined setup total.

success.description: No numerical finite-budget full-master-key success is established for this exact endpoint. The intermediate2^90.7-data analysis targets a fixed-wrong192-bit-guess survival of2^-43 and an expected2^149 survivors. The final2^89.1 endpoint reuses three overlapping column choices; no final joint elimination rate or stochastic independence is provided, so the intermediate2^-43 is not copied into its components. The64-bit residual completion is priced as expected work, not a recovery probability.

review.scope: Exact-edition endpoint-specific success audit; preserve resource parameters, existing conflicts and full-audit gates. Local source models and conditional relations do not certify whole-output success.

components.description: PDF6 Proposition1 and the source elimination rule: a true hypothesis cannot satisfy both conditions of the impossible differential and is not discarded by that mathematical contradiction. This is a local retention relation, not a finite-budget uniqueness or residual-search success rate.

PDF10–11: after a k7 hypothesis peels the last round, the inner attack requires eight zero-difference bytes, yielding expected2^57.7 pairs at the preliminary2^90.7 data budget. This is not an eight-round raw-ciphertext sieve or a final-data survivor count.
PDF11: each inner pair suggests an expected2^32 out of2^64 values of w6, i.e. source-model fraction2^-32. It is not a whole192-bit key survival probability.
